title: EU import requirements for certain dairy products and fishery products
summary: EU clarifies requirements for farmed bivalve molluscs, echinoderms, tunicates and marine gastropods, and food preparations based on …
update:
Regulation 2022/2292 establishes which animal products must meet public health requirements (hygiene requirements, residue control plans, approval of establishments and official certificates) to be exported to the European Union (EU).

The new Regulation 2026/1304 updates this list of products by adding food preparations based on dairy products (included in Combined Nomenclature /Harmonized System (CN/HS) customs code 1901) and fishery products (included in CN/HS 2103).

It also clarifies that live, chilled, frozen, and processed bivalve molluscs, echinoderms, tunicates, and marine gastropods farmed in the sea do not need to be included in control plans for residues, contaminants, and pesticide residues. This only applies where their production takes place in premises on land.
impacted_products: Food preparations based on dairy products and fishery products; live, chilled, frozen and processed bivalve molluscs, echinoderms, tunicates, and marine gastropods
timeline: The new rules apply from 13 September 2026 .
actions: Competent authorities in exporting countries may need to update certification procedures for animal products in the newly added CN categories.
background:
Regulation 2017/625 lays down rules for official controls to verify that animals and goods entering the EU comply with EU food and food safety requirements.

Regulation 2022/2292 supplements those rules for the entry into the EU of food-producing animals and certain goods intended for human consumption. It sets out the obligations for exporting countries to be listed in the Annexes to Regulation 2021/405 and to approve the operators exporting to the EU, and to lay down a control plan for pesticides, contaminants, and pharmacological substances. It also identifies the relevant products by CN or HS codes.

Regulation 853/2004 lays down specific hygiene rules for products of animal origin. It requires food business operators importing products of animal origin from non-EU countries to ensure that the country is listed for the product concerned, and that the establishment from which the product was dispatched, obtained, or prepared is also listed.

In September 2023, Regulation 2023/2652 amended and corrected Regulation 2022/2292 for honey, meat products, highly refined products, gelatine capsules, fishery products, and private attestations.

In January 2025, Regulation 2025/637 added certain dairy products, food additives derived from animals, and collagen casings with CN/HS customs codes 1301, 1806, 3203, 3204, 3823, 3824, 2202 99, and 3917 10 10 to the list of products that can only be imported from authorised non-EU countries. It introduced certain dairy products and collagen casings with customs codes 1806, 2202 99, and 3917 10 10 in the list of products that can only be exported from listed establishments.
